steps.title: From a point to a path

content.value:
A PathChain is a sequence of paths the Follower executes one after another. The robot completes segment 1, then smoothly transitions to segment 2.

You build one with follower.pathBuilder(), chaining .addPath() and .set*HeadingInterpolation() calls, then .build().

Always call .setGlobalDeceleration() before .build() — it's more optimized than the default deceleration, even for single-path chains.

Starting from the field center (70.75, 70.75) facing 90° (up). Here's a two-segment chain:

PathChain chain = follower.pathBuilder()
    .addPath(new BezierLine(
        new Pose(70.75, 70.75, 0),
        new Pose(70.75, 118.75, 0)
    ))
    .setConstantHeadingInterpolation(0)
    .addPath(new BezierLine(
        new Pose(70.75, 118.75, 0),
        new Pose(34.75, 118.75, 0)
    ))
    .setConstantHeadingInterpolation(0)
    .setGlobalDeceleration()
    .build();

Segment 1 drives forward 48". Segment 2 strafes left 36". setConstantHeadingInterpolation keeps the robot facing right the whole time.

Run it with: schedule(new FollowPathCommand(follower, chain))

Open PathChainOpMode.java.

The skeleton has a private Follower field and empty initialize().

Create the Follower with Constants.createFollower(hardwareMap). Set its pose with follower.setPose(new Pose(70.75, 70.75, 0)).

Position the robot before starting: left-click drag near center, right-click to set heading to 0° (right).

Build a PathChain with three BezierLine segments starting from the field center:

Segment 1: (70.75, 70.75, 0) to (118.75, 70.75, 0) — 48" forward.

Segment 2: (118.75, 70.75, 0) to (118.75, 106.75, 0) — 36" left.

Segment 3: (118.75, 106.75, 0) to (70.75, 70.75, 0) — return.

Use setConstantHeadingInterpolation(0) on each. End with .setGlobalDeceleration().

Schedule: new FollowPathCommand(follower, chain).
Start the OpMode. The Follower drives all three segments in sequence. If it overshoots, the PIDF gains in Constants.java need adjustment.
